spec.verdict:
YES for 860 of 873 — but only if four rendering rules are adopted first, and only if stretches get a third state. The wrongness the six reports found lives overwhelmingly in the RENDERER, not in free-exercise-db.

WHAT I RE-VERIFIED FROM THE REPO (node over site/exercises.js and site/data.js, deterministic, not sampled): 873 exercises; exactly 17 distinct muscle strings; primaryMuscles length distribution is {1:873} — there is never a second primary; 272 exercises have an empty secondaryMuscles array; kind = {strengthen:750, stretch:91, mobility:32}; category = {strength 581, stretching 123, plyometrics 61, powerlifting 38, olympic weightlifting 35, strongman 21, cardio 14}. The 17 strings map 1:1 and totally onto the 17 authored pages in window.RNAWIKI_DATA.anatomy.muscles (bridged by db_name on exactly 'lower back' and 'middle back'). That join is complete in both directions. Every count in the VOCABULARY report reproduced exactly; every count in the shoulder-arm report that its reviewer disputed reproduced on the reviewer's side, not the auditor's (bench family = 37 rows, 25 chest / 12 triceps, not 31 rows 19/12).

THE RECONCILIATION THAT MAKES THIS BUILDABLE. Both the shoulder-arm agent and the vocabulary agent graded "shoulders", "traps", "forearms" and "calves" as blocks-the-diagram because a single blob would paint the wrong face of the body. Their reviewer was right and the generalisation is the whole spec: a front/back inversion only happens if you CHOOSE to draw a wrapping muscle on one face. The deltoid genuinely wraps the joint; the trapezius genuinely runs occiput to T12; the forearm genuinely has two compartments on opposite surfaces. Draw each on BOTH figures and none of them is wrong — merely coarse. That single decision converts three of the four "blockers" (17 rear-delt ids, 5 palms-down wrist curls, Scapular_Pull-Up and the mid/lower trapezius) from wrong answers into acceptable coarseness, with no data change at all. The fourth — calves — does not survive it, because 6 exercises tagged 'calves' are on the front or the outside of the shin or on the sole of the foot, and drawing the whole lower leg on both figures would light the shin for all 22 real calf raises. That one needs data.

THE FOUR RULES (non-negotiable; each one, if broken, converts a coarse page into a confidently wrong one):
R1 — A muscle that wraps or spans both surfaces is drawn on BOTH figures. Applies to deltoid, trapezius, forearm, neck, outer hip, inner thigh. Never one face only.
R2 — The trapezius shape is the full occiput-to-T12 diamond, never the neck-to-shoulder slope. StatPearls NBK518994: upper fibres elevate, middle retract, lower depress. Shrunk to the slope, Scapular_Pull-Up ("depressing your shoulder girdle in a reverse shrugging motion") highlights its own antagonist. Full diamond and it is simply correct.
R3 — Depth is not drawable. A shape claims a SURFACE, not a volume. Anything deep to a superficial muscle (brachialis under biceps, pec minor under pec major, rhomboids under trapezius — StatPearls NBK534856: "immediately deep to the trapezius", transversus abdominis, iliopsoas, the whole rotator cuff) shares the superficial muscle's pixels and must be named in the LABEL. It never gets its own fill.
R4 — No shape may be lit by data that cannot distinguish it. The 17 strings contain zero sub-part information. Anterior vs posterior deltoid, upper vs lower trapezius, flexor vs extensor compartment, gastrocnemius vs tibialis anterior — none of these is derivable from primaryMuscles. Any region finer than the 17 must be dark until a per-exercise sidecar names it. Building sub-part shapes on top of a coarse tag is exactly the "confident wrong answer on 873 pages" the founder is trying to avoid.

THE 13 EXCEPTIONS — pages where Layer 1 would paint a body part that is not doing the work. These must be suppressed (render the text list, no figure) or corrected in a sidecar before launch: Anterior_Tibialis-SMR, Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises, Peroneals-SMR, Peroneals_Stretch, Foot-SMR, Knee_Circles, Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation, Dumbbell_Lying_Supination, Lower_Back_Curl, Barbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise, Dumbbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise, Smith_Incline_Shoulder_Raise, Crossover_Reverse_Lunge. That is 1.5% of the corpus, and each is verifiable from the exercise's own instruction text without any external source.

WHERE A DIAGRAM IS DISHONEST AND MUST NOT BE DRAWN AT ALL — carrying the shoulder-arm reviewer's verdict forward rather than averaging it: the ROTATOR CUFF. Subscapularis sits on the costal (rib-facing) surface of the scapula; every pixel above it on a front silhouette is ribcage and pectoral, and on a back view it is hidden by the scapula itself. Infraspinatus and teres minor sit in the posterior fossae under the deltoid and trapezius. On a 380x440 two-figure silhouette there is no honest pixel for any of them. The 7 cuff exercises (External_Rotation, External_Rotation_with_Band, External_Rotation_with_Cable, Cable_Internal_Rotation, Internal_Rotation_with_Band, Reverse_Flyes_With_External_Rotation, Cuban_Press) get a labelled callout — "deep muscles behind/under the shoulder blade — not visible on a body outline" — not a fill. Silently filling the deltoid cap for them is a fabricated location.

TWO THINGS THAT ARE NOT FIXABLE BY DRAWING, AND ONE OF THEM BLOCKS LAUNCH:
(1) STRETCH SEMANTICS — BLOCKS. 123 pages (category='stretching') where the tagged muscle is being lengthened or compressed, not producing force. One colour cannot mean "this muscle is producing the force" on 750 pages and "this muscle is being pulled long" on 123. Detail in stretch_vs_strengthen.
(2) SAME MOVEMENT, DIFFERENT HIGHLIGHT — 134 exercises. The deadlift family splits 12 hamstrings / 8 lower back / 6 quadriceps. The clean-and-snatch family splits 20 hamstrings / 11 quadriceps / 7 shoulders / 2 traps / 1 forearms. The upright row splits 3 shoulders / 4 traps on near-verbatim identical prose. Bench/floor/board/pin/chest press splits 25 chest / 12 triceps. Good morning splits 5 hamstrings / 2 lower back. Chin-up splits 8 lats / 1 middle back / 1 traps. No single page here is provably wrong — the reviewer was right that %MVIC cannot rank muscles against each other and that PMID 37229415's own conclusion declines to — but a reader who opens Barbell_Deadlift (lower back lit) and then Trap_Bar_Deadlift (front of thigh lit) sees the site contradict itself. On a health site that reads as unreliability. This is a sidecar job, not a renderer job.

THE 2D ASSET ALREADY EXISTS AND THE SHOULDER-ARM AGENT MISSED IT. window.RNAWIKI_DATA.bodyZones: viewBox "0 0 380 440", two figures at ox=10 and ox=200, a 10-shape silhouette, 15 zones; plus window.RNAWIKI_DATA.bodyWhereSvg, a prebuilt 9,007-char SVG, inlined server-side into site/where.html (20 bw-sil shapes present in the static HTML), with a 5,190-char bodyWhereIndex text fallback carrying real <a href> links. Reuse the geometry and the accessibility pattern; replace the zones array. See accessibility.

regions.label: Neck
regions.note: LAYER 1 (derivable from the tag, ships day one). Front = sternocleidomastoid, the cord from behind the ear to the collarbone; back = splenius/upper cervical extensors. Both faces per R1. 8 primary, 1 secondary — the smallest region in the corpus and the only one where the DB's 'neck' string and the anatomy agree without argument. On the existing silhouette this is the 18x14 neck rect at y63-77, 16x13 CSS px at scale 1.0 — big enough for one fill, nothing finer.

regions.label: Top of the shoulders and the diamond down the middle of the back
regions.note: LAYER 1. MUST be the full occiput-to-T12 diamond (R2), not the neck slope. Front figure gets only the visible neck-to-shoulder slope; back figure gets the whole diamond. StatPearls NBK518994: upper fibres elevate and upwardly rotate, middle retract, lower depress and assist upward rotation. Drawn as the full diamond, Scapular_Pull-Up is coarse but correct, not inverted — this is the shoulder-arm reviewer's correction and I am carrying it. DECLARED MERGE: levator scapulae is filed in the repo under groupId 'traps' (structures row FMA:32519, region 'neck-posterior') and is a separate muscle, not a trapezius part; it shares these pixels under R3 and must be named in the label copy, not given a shape. COLLISION: see interscapular.

regions.label: Shoulder cap
regions.note: LAYER 1, and the single most consequential shape in the spec — 'shoulders' is the largest tag at 127 primary / 209 secondary / 336 total. Drawn on BOTH figures per R1, it is honest for all 127. Drawn front-only it inverts 17 rear-delt exercises by the full depth of the body (StatPearls NBK537056: anterior part flexes the arm, posterior part extends it — directly opposing). Geometry: on the existing silhouette this is the top of the arm rect (x31-48, y75-102) plus the outer top corner of the torso, about 21x27 base units = 19x24 CSS px at scale 1.0. That is enough for ONE shape and not three; three deltoid heads at this size would be ~7px each. Do not attempt them from the tag (R4).

regions.label: Chest
regions.note: LAYER 1. Pectoralis major over the upper ribcage, front only. StatPearls NBK525991: flexion, adduction and medial rotation of the arm at the glenohumeral joint. 84 primary, 63 secondary. DECLARED MERGE under R3: pectoralis minor lies directly beneath and occupies the same pixels (repo structures row FMA:13109, region 'chest-deep'); name it in the label. Note the existing /where map already has a 'chest' zone carrying muscleGroup:'chest' — the only zone in the whole bodyZones array with a muscleGroup field, i.e. the hook for this join is already half-built.

regions.label: Abdominal wall — the midline and the sides of the waist
regions.note: LAYER 1. Rectus abdominis down the midline plus the external obliques wrapping the flanks; front only. 93 primary, 56 secondary. DECLARED MERGE under R3: transversus abdominis is the deepest layer and shares these pixels (repo row FMA:15570, region 'trunk-anterior-deep') — it is the only muscle actually working in Stomach_Vacuum. UPGRADE AVAILABLE: 19 abdominals-primary exercises are rotation or side-bend movements (obliques) rather than midline flexion; a separate flank shape is genuinely drawable on the 62x92 torso rect, but it is sidecar-only under R4 because the tag is identical for both.

regions.label: Front of the upper arm
regions.note: LAYER 1. 53 primary, 74 secondary. DECLARED MERGE AND UNAVOIDABLE under R3: brachialis lies directly deep to biceps brachii and occupies identical pixels on any silhouette (the repo carries it as its own structure, FMA:37667, region 'upper-arm-anterior-deep'). The label must name both, or the site silently misattributes 5 reverse curls and 6 hammer curls whose prime mover is brachialis/brachioradialis. Geometry: upper half of the 17x118 arm rect, ~15 CSS px wide at scale 1.0 — one shape only. Brachioradialis is NOT separately drawable here at any realistic render size; the shoulder-arm agent's 20px estimate was derived from invented proportions, not from this asset. Note the biceps-brachii structures row has an EMPTY fma field, so any FMA-keyed join fails on this region.

regions.label: Back of the upper arm
regions.note: LAYER 1. 71 primary, 147 secondary. MERGE ACCEPTED AND FREE: long, lateral and medial heads are one shape, and unlike the deltoid and trapezius merges this one costs nothing — no exercise in the 873 distinguishes them. Worth one line of label copy: only the long head crosses the shoulder, which is why overhead extensions differ from pushdowns.

regions.label: Forearm
regions.note: LAYER 1. 25 primary, 94 secondary. Drawn on BOTH figures per R1 and labelled just 'forearm', this is coarse but never wrong. Drawn on one face only it puts either the 7 palms-up wrist curls or the 5 palms-down wrist curls on the wrong surface of the limb (StatPearls NBK539784: anterior compartment flexes the wrist and digits, posterior compartment extends). Note the shoulder-arm agent corrected the vocabulary agent here and was right: pronator teres and pronator quadratus are ANTERIOR, only supinator is posterior — a 'pronation goes on the back' assumption is inverted. The existing silhouette's arm is a straight 17x118 rect with no hand and no rotation, so there is no palms-forward/palms-to-thighs problem to solve; the pose is abstract. DECLARED MERGE: brachioradialis shares these pixels.

regions.label: Broad muscle down the side and lower half of the back
regions.note: LAYER 1. 38 primary, 56 secondary. StatPearls NBK448120: 'a broad, flat muscle occupying most of the lower posterior thorax', origin from T6-S5 spinous processes and thoracolumbar fascia, posterior iliac crest and lower 3-4 ribs, inserting on the floor of the intertubercular sulcus; acts to adduct, medially rotate and extend the humerus. Back only — the belly is entirely posterior even though the tendon wraps to the front of the humerus. OVERLAP, unavoidable and honest: it lies over the lower trapezius and over the erector spinae. Under R3 that is a shared-surface fact to state in the label, not a reason to shrink the shape.

regions.label: Between the shoulder blades
regions.note: LAYER 1, and the one genuine geometric collision in the spec. 34 primary, 64 secondary. The authored middle-back page's own group string is 'Rhomboids (major & minor), middle trapezius' while the traps page claims 'Trapezius (upper, middle, lower fibres)' — two regions claiming the same anatomy, verified from the repo. StatPearls NBK534856 settles the geometry, not the ownership: the rhomboids are 'immediately deep to the trapezius', so on a 2D back view these ARE the same pixels. 32 exercises name both traps and middle back. RESOLUTION TO ADOPT: give trapezius the full diamond as a fill, and draw interscapular as a nested inner shape with a different treatment (outline, hatch, or a darker tone) rather than a competing fill. On the 62x92 torso rect the inner shape is roughly 36x27 base units — legible at scale 1.0, illegible below about 300 CSS px total width, where it must collapse into trapezius.

regions.label: Lower back
regions.note: LAYER 1. 27 primary, 104 secondary. Erector spinae columns either side of the lumbar spine. StatPearls NBK537074: iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis are the intermediate group and 'only the intrinsic muscles are considered true back muscles' — trapezius, latissimus dorsi, levator scapulae and rhomboids are named as EXTRINSIC muscles that move the upper limb. That is the cleanest available justification for keeping this shape distinct from lats and trapezius even though they overlap it. DECLARED MERGE: multifidus and quadratus lumborum (repo rows FMA:22827 and FMA:15569) are deep to it and share its pixels.

regions.label: Glutes
regions.note: LAYER 1. 22 primary but 220 secondary — the second most-referenced string in the corpus, and on 174 pages it co-occurs with quadriceps. Maps onto the 54x44 pelvis rect on the back figure. DECLARED MERGE: gluteus maximus (superficial) over medius and minimus (deep, repo rows FMA:22315 and FMA:22317). Note the existing /where map already has a 'glutes' back zone at cx80 cy184 rx24 ry15 — reusable geometry.

regions.label: Outer hip
regions.note: LAYER 1. 8 primary, 35 secondary — the smallest primary count after neck. Gluteus medius/minimus and tensor fasciae latae on the lateral hip; visible on the outer edge of both figures, so BOTH per R1. Geometry is tight: the outer sliver of the 54x44 pelvis rect, roughly 8 base units wide. Below ~300 CSS px this should merge into glutes rather than render as an unreadable 5px strip. Caveat for the label: Iliotibial_Tract-SMR rolls the IT band, which is fascia, not a muscle.

regions.label: Inner thigh
regions.note: LAYER 1. 14 primary, 41 secondary. The medial edge of the thigh is visible on both figures, so BOTH per R1. Geometry: the inner ~7 base units of the 22-wide leg rect, i.e. about 6 CSS px at scale 1.0. This is the region most at risk of illegibility — set a hard minimum render width (see accessibility) below which it merges into the thigh shape rather than drawing a strip nobody can see.

regions.label: Front of the thigh
regions.note: LAYER 1, and the largest primary tag in the corpus at 147 primary / 82 secondary. Maps onto the front figure's 22x182 leg rect above the knee. The existing /where map already has a 'Front of thigh' zone at cx67/93 cy248 rx11 ry26 — directly reusable. IMPORTANT NUANCE that stops an over-claim: 8 quadriceps-primary exercises are hip-flexion movements (Hip_Flexion_with_Band, Standing_Hip_Flexors, Kneeling_Hip_Flexor, Rear_Leg_Raises, Looking_At_Ceiling, One_Half_Locust, Iron_Crosses_stretch, Intermediate_Hip_Flexor_and_Quad_Stretch) whose dominant muscle is iliopsoas — StatPearls NBK531508: psoas major, psoas minor and iliacus, 'the primary flexor of the thigh', lying 'posteriorly within the retroperitoneum', inserting on the lesser trochanter. But StatPearls NBK513334 confirms rectus femoris is a quadriceps muscle that DOES cross the hip and flex it. So the anterior-thigh shape is adjacent and partially correct, not inverted. This is coarseness, not a defect — do NOT list these as bad data.

regions.label: Back of the thigh
regions.note: LAYER 1. 79 primary, 201 secondary. Back figure, leg rect above the knee. The /where map's 'Back of thigh' zone is directly reusable. DECLARED MERGE: biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus are one shape; no exercise in the 873 distinguishes them.

regions.label: Calf
regions.note: LAYER 1, AND THE ONE REGION WHERE R1 DOES NOT RESCUE THE TAG. Gastrocnemius and soleus on the BACK of the lower leg only. 28 primary, 181 secondary. Drawing 'calves' on both figures to be safe would be worse, not better: it would light the shin on all 22 genuine calf raises. So this shape stays back-only and the 6 exercises that are not on the back of the calf must be handled in the sidecar (see known_bad_tagging). The repo already carries the fix half-built: structures row 'tibialis-anterior' (FMA:22532, region 'lower-leg-anterior') exists under its own groupId with NO authored muscle page and NO exercise-DB string — it is an orphan waiting for exactly this.

regions.label: Front of the shoulder
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR ONLY, DARK UNTIL AUTHORED. Not derivable from the tag (R4): all 127 shoulders-primary exercises carry the identical string. Once a sidecar exists this is the correct shape for presses and front raises. Anatomy: StatPearls NBK537056, anterior (clavicular) part, 'works with the pectoralis major to flex the arm'. Geometry warning: splitting the 21x27-base-unit deltoid cap into front and back halves is only legible at scale 1.0 or better; below ~340 CSS px total width, collapse to the single deltoid shape.

regions.label: Back of the shoulder
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR ONLY. The posterior (spinal) part, which 'works with the latissimus dorsi to extend the arm' (NBK537056). The 17 rear-delt ids the shoulder-arm reviewer enumerated are its population: Reverse_Flyes, Reverse_Machine_Flyes, Reverse_Flyes_With_External_Rotation, Face_Pull, Band_Pull_Apart, Back_Flyes_-_With_Bands, Barbell_Rear_Delt_Row, Cable_Rear_Delt_Fly, Cable_Rope_Rear-Delt_Rows, Bent_Over_Dumbbell_Rear_Delt_Raise_With_Head_On_Bench, Bent_Over_Low-Pulley_Side_Lateral, Seated_Bent-Over_Rear_Delt_Raise, Dumbbell_Lying_One-Arm_Rear_Lateral_Raise, Dumbbell_Lying_Rear_Lateral_Raise, Lying_Rear_Delt_Raise, Sled_Reverse_Flye, Low_Pulley_Row_To_Neck. Under R1 these are already NOT wrong on Layer 1 — the both-faces deltoid covers them. This region is a precision upgrade, not a bug fix.

regions.label: Deep muscles around the shoulder blade
regions.note: NOT A SILHOUETTE FILL — A LABELLED CALLOUT. This is the one place I am carrying a reviewer's 'dishonest' verdict forward without softening it. Subscapularis lies on the costal (rib-facing) surface of the scapula (StatPearls NBK441844); infraspinatus and teres minor lie in the posterior fossae under the deltoid and trapezius. There is no honest pixel for any of them on a 380x440 two-figure outline. Teres minor is absent from all 43 structures rows entirely (verified). The 7 pages that need it — External_Rotation, External_Rotation_with_Band, External_Rotation_with_Cable, Cable_Internal_Rotation, Internal_Rotation_with_Band, Reverse_Flyes_With_External_Rotation, Cuban_Press — get the deltoid shape shown at reduced emphasis plus the sentence 'the working muscles here sit deep under the shoulder blade and are not visible on a body outline'. Filling the deltoid cap and saying nothing would be a fabricated location.

regions.label: Fan over the side ribs, below the armpit
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR ONLY. Prime mover of the 3 incline shoulder raises, whose own text says 'lift the bar by protracting your shoulder blades'. StatPearls NBK531457: origin ribs 1-8/9, insertion along the medial border of the scapula, 'pulls the scapula forward around the thorax'. It is on the RIBCAGE, not the shoulder, so it is a different body segment from any deltoid shape. The shoulder-arm agent claimed no correct answer was reachable because serratus-anterior is filed under groupId 'chest'; its reviewer was right that the three exercises already carry 'chest' as a secondary, so a renderer that resolves secondaries lands on the right group with no schema change. Geometry: an 8-base-unit strip on each lateral edge of the 62-wide torso rect, ~7 CSS px — legible only at scale 1.0 or above.

regions.label: Palm side of the forearm
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR ONLY. Anterior compartment: flexes the wrist and fingers (StatPearls NBK539784). Population is the 7 palms-up wrist curls plus all grip work. Under R1 these are already not wrong on Layer 1; this is precision, not a fix.

regions.label: Back of the forearm
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR ONLY. Posterior compartment: extends the wrist and fingers. Population is the 5 palms-down wrist curls (Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Bench, Palms-Down_Dumbbell_Wrist_Curl_Over_A_Bench, Seated_Dumbbell_Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl, Seated_One-Arm_Dumbbell_Palms-Down_Wrist_Curl, Seated_Palms-Down_Barbell_Wrist_Curl). Corrected count is 5, not the vocabulary agent's 6 — its sixth member, Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation, is not a forearm exercise at all.

regions.label: Front of the shin
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR REQUIRED, AND THE ONLY LAYER 2 REGION THAT FIXES A REAL WRONG ANSWER RATHER THAN ADDING PRECISION. Tibialis anterior is the direct antagonist of the calf: StatPearls NBK539725, 'the strongest dorsiflexor', anterior compartment, opposite action to plantarflexion. Needed by Anterior_Tibialis-SMR and Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises. The repo already has the structures row (FMA:22532, region 'lower-leg-anterior') with its own groupId, no muscle page and no exercise string — it exists solely to serve this case. Geometry is comfortable: the front figure's 22x182 leg rect below the knee.

regions.label: Outside of the shin
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR REQUIRED. Lateral compartment: fibularis (peroneus) longus and brevis, evertors, 'explicitly lateral compartment muscles, not posterior/calf muscles', separated from the posterior compartments by intermuscular septa (StatPearls NBK519526). Needed by Peroneals-SMR and Peroneals_Stretch. Visible on the outer edge of both figures. Note the DB gets the stretch directions right — Peroneals_Stretch inverts the foot (correct for stretching evertors) and Posterior_Tibialis_Stretch everts it (correct for stretching an invertor) — so only the muscle NAME is misfiled, not the mechanics.

regions.label: Sides of the waist
regions.note: LAYER 2 — SIDECAR ONLY, OPTIONAL. 19 abdominals-primary exercises are rotation or lateral-flexion movements (Russian_Twist, Barbell_Side_Bend, Dumbbell_Side_Bend, Plate_Twist, Cable_Russian_Twists, Oblique_Crunches, Decline_Oblique_Crunch, Standing_Cable_Wood_Chop, Landmine_180s, the three kettlebell windmills, Seated_Barbell_Twist, Medicine_Ball_Full_Twist, One-Arm_High-Pulley_Cable_Side_Bends, Weighted_Ball_Side_Bend, Torso_Rotation, Side_Bridge, Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Bends). The flank is a genuinely different place from the midline six-pack and is drawable on the 62-wide torso rect. Lowest priority of the Layer 2 set: the coarse abdominal-wall shape already covers the obliques, so this is refinement, not correction.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: 'calves' is used for the whole lower leg and foot. 6 exercises tagged calves-primary are on the FRONT of the shin (the direct antagonist), the OUTSIDE of the shin (a separate compartment behind an intermuscular septum), the knee, or the sole of the foot. This is the one region where drawing on both figures does not rescue the tag, because doing so would light the shin on all 22 genuine calf raises. Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises is the sharpest case and needs no external source: its own text says 'Stand on the platform with the heels of your feet secured on top of it with the balls of your feet extending off... Raise the balls of your feet as you breathe out by extending your toes as high as possible' — that is dorsiflexion, i.e. tibialis anterior — while the same sentence then says 'and flexing your calf', which contradicts the motion it just described.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Retag to a new drawable region. Anterior_Tibialis-SMR and Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises -> shin-front (the repo already carries structures row tibialis-anterior, FMA:22532, region 'lower-leg-anterior', currently an orphan with no muscle page and no exercise string). Peroneals-SMR and Peroneals_Stretch -> outer-shin (StatPearls NBK519526: fibularis longus and brevis, evertors, 'lateral compartment muscles, not posterior/calf muscles'). Foot-SMR -> suppress the figure entirely; it is plantar fascia on the sole of the foot and the silhouette has only a 13x8 foot ellipse. Knee_Circles -> suppress; it is a knee mobility drill and the calf is not the working muscle. Sources: StatPearls NBK539725 (anterior compartment, 'the strongest dorsiflexor'), NBK519526 (lateral compartment), NBK537340 (posterior compartment = gastrocnemius, soleus, plantaris).

known_bad_tagging.pattern: WRONG LIMB SEGMENT. Two exercises are forearms-primary with no secondary muscles, and neither instruction describes forearm rotation. Both describe shoulder EXTERNAL ROTATION with the humerus fixed and the elbow at 90 degrees — the classic side-lying/prone rotator cuff drill. Verbatim from the repo, Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation step 4: 'As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted forward as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm.' Dumbbell_Lying_Supination is the same movement lying on the side. A forearm highlight is wrong by an entire limb segment and by front-versus-back. This also corrects the vocabulary agent, which counted Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation among posterior-forearm exercises.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Retag primary to the rotator-cuff callout, not to any fill. Prime movers are infraspinatus and teres minor on the posterior scapula (StatPearls NBK441844: 'The infraspinatus and teres minor function primarily as lateral (external) rotators'). Neither is drawable on a silhouette — infraspinatus lies under the deltoid and trapezius, and teres minor is absent from all 43 structures rows. Render the deltoid at reduced emphasis plus the deep-muscle sentence.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: THE TAG NAMES THE ANTAGONIST, PROVEN BY THE EXERCISE'S OWN TEXT. Lower_Back_Curl is abdominals-primary. Its instructions read verbatim: 'Lie on your stomach with your arms out to your sides... Using your lower back muscles, extend your spine lifting your chest off of the ground. Do not use your arms to push yourself up.' It is a prone back extension. The abdominal wall is the antagonist. It is also filed category='stretching' / kind='stretch' while prescribing 'Repeat for 10-20 repetitions'.
known_bad_tagging.correction: primary -> 'lower back' (erector spinae, back view). kind -> strengthen. This is the trunk equivalent of the Side_Wrist_Pull case the shoulder-arm reviewer found: an exercise whose own prose disowns its tag. Needs no external source.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: A PRIME MOVER ON A DIFFERENT BODY SEGMENT. The three incline shoulder raises are shoulders-primary and their instructions describe pure scapular PROTRACTION — Barbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise step 2 verbatim: 'While keeping the arms straight, lift the bar by protracting your shoulder blades, raising the shoulders from the bench.' The prime mover is serratus anterior, which is on the RIBCAGE under the armpit, not on the shoulder. A deltoid-cap highlight puts the reader's eye on a different body segment.
known_bad_tagging.correction: primary -> serratus region (front view, lateral ribcage). StatPearls NBK531457: origin ribs 1-8/9, insertion along the medial border of the scapula, 'pulls the scapula forward around the thorax'. IMPORTANT — the shoulder-arm agent claimed no correct answer was reachable because serratus-anterior is filed under groupId 'chest'; its reviewer refuted that and was right: all three exercises already carry 'chest' as a secondary muscle, so a renderer that resolves secondaries reaches the correct group with no schema change. Also drop Rack_Delivery from this set — its protraction sentence is a positional cue about where the bar rests, not the loaded action.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: A LOWER-LIMB MOVEMENT TAGGED TO THE TRUNK. Crossover_Reverse_Lunge is lower-back-primary. Its own text: 'Perform a rear lunge by stepping back with one foot and flexing the hips and front knee. As you do so, rotate your torso across the front leg.' The erector spinae is a stabiliser here, not the engine — and the engine is already sitting in its own secondaryMuscles array (abdominals, abductors, glutes, hamstrings, quadriceps).
known_bad_tagging.correction: primary -> quadriceps (or glutes). The data needed to fix this page is already inside the page. Self-correcting in any renderer that shows secondaries — which is an argument for showing them.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: NO DRAWABLE LOCATION EXISTS. 7 shoulders-primary exercises are rotator cuff movements. Subscapularis sits on the costal (rib-facing) surface of the scapula; infraspinatus and teres minor sit in the posterior fossae deep to the deltoid and trapezius. None has an honest pixel on a 380x440 two-figure outline, and teres minor is absent from all 43 structures rows entirely (verified by dump). NOTE — the shoulder-arm agent's reviewer was right to strike Cable_Internal_Rotation and Internal_Rotation_with_Band from its 'wrong side of the body' list: subscapularis is anterior, so an anterior highlight for internal rotation is not a front/back inversion. The problem with all 7 is DEPTH, not side.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Do not fill. Render the deltoid shape at reduced emphasis and add the sentence: 'The working muscles here sit deep under the shoulder blade and are not visible on a body outline.' Adding a fake fill is worse than adding nothing — this is the one place where the honest product decision is to show less.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: SAME MOVEMENT, THREE DIFFERENT HIGHLIGHTS — THE DEADLIFT. 26 deadlift and rack-pull rows split 12 hamstrings-primary / 8 lower-back-primary / 6 quadriceps-primary. Barbell_Deadlift lights the lower back; Trap_Bar_Deadlift lights the front of the thigh; Clean_Deadlift lights the back of the thigh. Some of the split is defensible by design (Romanian, stiff-legged and sumo variants are deliberately hamstring-biased), but Barbell_Deadlift vs Trap_Bar_Deadlift vs Cable_Deadlifts vs Leverage_Deadlift vs Rickshaw_Deadlift is not — nothing in the ids or the instruction text distinguishes them. This needs no external source and no EMG argument: it is the repo contradicting itself.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Pick ONE primary for the conventional hip-hinge pull and apply it to all of them in a sidecar. Do not attempt to settle it with EMG — the shoulder-arm reviewer correctly established that %MVIC is a within-muscle index that cannot rank force contribution between different muscles, and that PMID 37229415's own conclusion declines to rank. The value here is consistency, not a resolved physiology question. 15 of the 26 are arbitrary: the 8 lower-back rows, the 6 quadriceps rows, and Clean_Deadlift.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: SAME MOVEMENT, FIVE DIFFERENT HIGHLIGHTS — THE CLEAN AND SNATCH. 41 rows split 20 hamstrings / 11 quadriceps / 7 shoulders / 2 traps / 1 forearms. Hang_Clean lights the front of the thigh; Kettlebell_Hang_Clean lights the back of it. This is the largest single family inconsistency in the corpus. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE SHOULDER-ARM REPORT, which its reviewer refuted and I am carrying forward: the claim that all 23 'Olympic/ballistic' shoulders-primary lifts are wrong because 'the arms are passive' does NOT hold. About 18 of them finish with or hold the load locked out overhead, where the deltoid and triceps are genuine prime movers, and both Turkish get-ups say 'Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times' — shoulders-primary is correct on those, not a wrong answer. The valid subset is 3: Two-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean (ends at the rack, no overhead component at all), Kettlebell_Sumo_High_Pull, Bottoms-Up_Clean_From_The_Hang_Position.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Two separate jobs. (a) Consistency: pick one primary for the pull-from-floor phase and apply it across the 31 quadriceps/hamstrings rows. (b) Correctness: retag only the 3 valid cases to a hip-driven primary. Note that 21 of the 23 already carry a hip driver in secondaryMuscles, so a renderer that shows secondaries is largely self-correcting here. Also flag: Push_Press has an EMPTY instructions[] array — one of only 5 rows in all 873 — so no prose-based method can check it at all.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: SAME MOVEMENT, TWO DIFFERENT HIGHLIGHTS — THE UPRIGHT ROW. 7 rows: 3 shoulders-primary, 4 traps-primary. Upright_Barbell_Row and Upright_Cable_Row carry near-verbatim identical cue text ('Use your side shoulders to lift... your elbows should always be higher than your forearms') and get different answers. The reader sees the shoulder cap lit on one page and the top of the back on the next. This is the cleanest proven internal contradiction in the shoulder-arm report and it survived audit intact.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Pick one and apply to all 7. Both muscles are genuinely loaded, so this is a consistency decision, not an anatomy one. Do not lean on PMID 18339796 to settle it: the shoulder-arm agent's supporting claim that 'every lateral raise in this DB is shoulders-primary with traps not even listed as secondary' is false — 3 of 11 lateral raises do list traps as secondary (Bent_Over_Low-Pulley_Side_Lateral, Cable_Seated_Lateral_Raise, Side_Laterals_to_Front_Raise), and that study is 12 women with diagnosed trapezius myalgia lifting 3-10 kg, a pain population at low load.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: SAME MOVEMENT, TWO DIFFERENT HIGHLIGHTS — THE HORIZONTAL PRESS. 37 bench/floor/board/pin/chest-press rows split 25 chest-primary / 12 triceps-primary. Most of the split is defensible: Close-Grip_Barbell_Bench_Press and Smith_Machine_Close-Grip_Bench_Press are close-grip by name, and Board_Press, Pin_Presses, Floor_Press, Floor_Press_with_Chains, Dumbbell_Floor_Press and One_Arm_Floor_Press are deliberately ROM-restricted to the lockout portion where the triceps is the recognised limiting factor. THE ARBITRARY RESIDUE IS 4. I am explicitly retracting the shoulder-arm report's version of this finding: its counts were wrong (it said 31 rows and 19 chest; the true figures are 37 and 25), its claim that three rows 'explicitly prescribe a competition-legal WIDE grip' misreads a permissive clause ('However wide your grip, it should cover the ring on the bar') as a prescription while dropping the triceps-biased cue in the same paragraph ('The elbows should be tucked in until lockout'), and its EMG argument is methodologically invalid.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Retag only the 4 full-ROM rows to chest-primary for consistency with the other 25, and leave the ROM-restricted and close-grip rows as triceps-primary. Diagram consequence is small either way: chest is front-view and triceps is back-view, so on these 4 pages the highlight currently appears on the opposite side of the body from the 25 near-identical pages beside them.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: SMALLER SAME-MOVEMENT SPLITS. Good morning: 5 hamstrings-primary vs 2 lower-back-primary, and the split runs backwards — Stiff_Leg_Barbell_Good_Morning, the most hamstring-biased variant by design, is one of the two tagged lower back. Chin-up: 8 lats-primary vs 1 middle-back (One_Arm_Chin-Up) vs 1 traps (Scapular_Pull-Up, which is a different movement and correctly tagged); Mixed_Grip_Chin is also middle-back-primary with lats demoted to secondary. Shrug: 9 traps-primary is consistent — Middle_Back_Shrug is NOT a defect despite the name, because its own text says 'squeeze your shoulder blades together', which is genuinely rhomboid and middle trapezius.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Good morning -> all 7 to one primary. Chin-up -> Mixed_Grip_Chin and One_Arm_Chin-Up to lats, matching the other 8 and matching their own secondaryMuscles which already list lats. Leave Middle_Back_Shrug and Scapular_Pull-Up alone; both are correctly tagged and only look wrong from their names.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: TWO REGIONS CLAIM THE SAME PIXELS. The authored middle-back page's group string is 'Rhomboids (major & minor), middle trapezius' while the traps page's is 'Trapezius (upper, middle, lower fibres)' — verified from window.RNAWIKI_DATA.anatomy.muscles. StatPearls NBK534856 confirms the geometry is not negotiable: the rhomboids are 'immediately deep to the trapezius'. 32 exercises name both strings, so the collision fires on 32 pages. This is a content-ownership defect, not a tagging defect, and it must be settled before any shape is drawn.
known_bad_tagging.correction: Give trapezius the full occiput-to-T12 diamond as the fill and draw interscapular as a NESTED inner shape with a different visual treatment (outline or hatch), never a competing fill. When both fire, the primary is filled and the secondary is outlined. Below about 300 CSS px of total map width, collapse interscapular into trapezius rather than render an illegible inner shape. Separately, edit one of the two authored group strings so the site stops claiming the middle trapezius twice.

known_bad_tagging.pattern: RENDERER PRECEDENCE HOLES. (a) 9 exercises list the SAME muscle in both primaryMuscles and secondaryMuscles, so without a rule the same shape is painted twice or flickers between the two colours. (b) 5 exercises have an EMPTY instructions[] array, so no prose-based verification of their tags is possible at all and no audit round can check them. (c) Standing_Olympic_Plate_Hand_Squeeze lists biceps as a secondary for a movement that is purely finger flexion ('Lower the plates until the fingers are nearly extended... raise the plates back by closing your hands') — it would put a second highlight on the upper arm for a grip exercise.
known_bad_tagging.correction: (a) Primary always wins; drop the duplicate from the secondary set before rendering. (b) Flag the 5 as unverified in the sidecar so no future audit reports them as checked. (c) Drop biceps from the hand-squeeze secondaries — biceps brachii crosses the elbow and shoulder, not the fingers; the finger flexors are flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus (StatPearls NBK539784).

known_bad_tagging.pattern: FINDINGS I AM EXPLICITLY REFUSING TO CARRY, so they do not get relitigated in a seventh round. (1) 'Reverse curls invert primary and secondary — brachioradialis becomes the prime mover.' Not supported by its own citations: PMID 36976950 shows brachioradialis excitation ALSO drops in pronation, and neither cited study makes a between-muscle comparison. Biceps brachii remains an elbow flexor in a reverse curl. The defensible version is that all 5 reverse curls and 6 hammer curls under-weight brachioradialis, which they already list as 'forearms' secondary — coarseness, not inversion. (2) 'Scapular_Pull-Up highlights its own antagonist.' Only true if the trapezius is drawn as a neck slope, which is a renderer mistake nobody has made yet; a correct full-diamond trapezius contains the lower fibres. (3) '59 of 91 stretches name their own primary muscle region in their instruction text.' Does not reproduce — 19 of 91 on a strict match, 35 on a deliberately generous stem map. (4) 'No 2D diagram exists.' It does: bodyZones plus bodyWhereSvg. (5) Hip-flexor exercises tagged quadriceps are NOT a defect: StatPearls NBK513334 confirms rectus femoris crosses the hip and flexes it, so the anterior-thigh shape is partially correct and merely coarse.
known_bad_tagging.correction: No data change. Recorded so the next audit does not re-raise them and so nobody spends a sidecar edit on a non-defect.

spec.stretch_vs_strengthen:
YES — the audits found it, and it is the one finding that genuinely blocks launch rather than merely needing a sidecar. But the honest version is THREE states, not two, and the field you would reach for first does not give them to you.

WHAT THE TAG MEANS ON A STRETCH. Across the stretch corpus the primary muscle is the one being LENGTHENED, not the one producing force. Triceps_Stretch ('Reach your hand behind your head, grasp your elbow and gently pull') is triceps-primary. Kneeling_Forearm_Stretch ('lean back keeping your palms flat on the floor until you feel a stretch in your wrists and forearms') is forearms-primary. So one highlight colour would carry two opposite physiological meanings across the same site: producing the force on 750 pages, being pulled long on 91. A reader cannot tell which from the picture.

THE FIELD YOU WOULD TRUST IS UNTRUSTWORTHY. `kind` is derived deterministically from `category` — every one of the 123 category='stretching' rows becomes kind='stretch' (91) or kind='mobility' (32), and no row outside that category becomes either. But `kind='mobility'` is a mixed shelf, verified by dumping all 32: it contains foam rolling (Calves-SMR, Lower_Back-SMR, Rhomboids-SMR, Peroneals-SMR, Brachialis-SMR), ordinary static stretches (Standing_Biceps_Stretch, Lying_Hamstring, Intermediate_Groin_Stretch), AND outright strengthening exercises (Superman, Frog_Hops, Split_Squats, Sit_Squats, Front_Leg_Raises, Rear_Leg_Raises, Side_Leg_Raises, Crossover_Reverse_Lunge, Shoulder_Raise — which is a shrug, while all 9 actual shrugs in the DB are traps-primary). Branching the diagram on `kind` reproduces the shelving error on the page.

THE PARTITION THAT DOES WORK. Recomputed from site/exercises.js, the 123 category='stretching' rows split cleanly and exhaustively on two fields that are already present — `force` and `equipment`:
  80 = force 'static' and not foam roll -> PASSIVE LENGTHENING. The tagged muscle is being pulled long.
  14 = equipment 'foam roll' or 'SMR' in the id -> COMPRESSION. Adductor, Anterior_Tibialis-SMR, Brachialis-SMR, Calves-SMR, Foot-SMR, Hamstring-SMR, Iliotibial_Tract-SMR, Latissimus_Dorsi-SMR, Lower_Back-SMR, Neck-SMR, Peroneals-SMR, Piriformis-SMR, Quadriceps-SMR, Rhomboids-SMR. The tissue is neither shortening nor lengthening — it is being pressed. Calling this 'stretched' is a third wrong answer, and the shoulder-arm reviewer was right to catch Brachialis-SMR being described as a stretch.
  29 = force 'push' or 'pull' -> ACTIVE MOVEMENT. Arm_Circles, Shoulder_Circles, Elbow_Circles, Wrist_Circles, Knee_Circles, Ankle_Circles, Standing_Hip_Circles, Hip_Circles_prone, Toe_Touchers, Torso_Rotation, Windmills, Iron_Crosses_stretch, Scissor_Kick, Groiners, Inchworm, Frog_Hops, Sit_Squats, Split_Squats, Rear_Leg_Raises, Front_Leg_Raises, Side_Leg_Raises, Shoulder_Raise, Shoulder_Stretch, Dynamic_Back_Stretch, Dynamic_Chest_Stretch, 90_90_Hamstring, Leg-Up_Hamstring_Stretch, Lying_Prone_Quadriceps, Crossover_Reverse_Lunge. Here the tagged muscle is CONTRACTING through range, or contracting and lengthening alternately.
80 + 14 + 29 = 123 exactly. No leftovers, no double-counting, both figures reproduce on re-run.

WHAT THE DIAGRAM MUST DO. Three visual states, not two colours:
  WORKING (solid fill) — 750 strengthen rows plus the 29 active rows. Caption: 'Muscles doing the work.'
  LENGTHENING (outline or hatched fill, same hue, no solid) — the 80 passive rows. Caption: 'Muscles being stretched.' The visual difference must be a different TREATMENT, not a different hue: hue is already carrying primary-vs-secondary, and stacking two meanings on one channel is how you end up with a legend nobody reads.
  PRESSED (a dot or marker at the region, no fill) — the 14 SMR rows. Caption: 'Where the roller goes.' A fill implies contraction or lengthening; neither is happening.
The caption is not decoration — it is the part a screen reader and a no-JS reader actually receive, and it is the only thing that makes the highlight unambiguous.

TWO EDGE CASES TO NAME RATHER THAN AVERAGE AWAY. (1) Seated_Biceps and Overhead_Triceps are PNF contract-relax drills in which the muscle both contracts and is stretched; either state is half right. Give them the LENGTHENING state and a one-line note. (2) 12 strengthen-category exercises carry explicit stretch language in their own text (Bent-Arm_Barbell_Pullover, Bent-Arm_Dumbbell_Pullover, Cable_Crossover, Decline_Dumbbell_Flyes, Dumbbell_Flyes, Incline_Cable_Flye, One-Arm_Flat_Bench_Dumbbell_Flye, Straight-Arm_Dumbbell_Pullover, Stiff-Legged_Barbell_Deadlift, Stiff-Legged_Dumbbell_Deadlift, Smith_Machine_Stiff-Legged_Deadlift, Weighted_Sissy_Squat). These are loaded-stretch strengthening movements and stay in the WORKING state — the stretch is a cue about position, not the training effect.

FINALLY, ONE CLAIM I AM RETRACTING ON BEHALF OF THE AUDITS. The shoulder-arm report justified its stretch design on '59 of 91 stretches name their own primary muscle region in their instruction text.' That does not reproduce: 19 of 91 on a strict match, 35 on a deliberately generous stem map. Its own worked example refutes it — Triceps_Stretch's text ('Reach your hand behind your head, grasp your elbow and gently pull') names neither the triceps nor its region. So you cannot lift the caption out of the instruction prose for most stretches; the state has to come from the force/equipment partition above.
spec.accessibility:
THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS UNUSUALLY GOOD NEWS: the exercise diagram needs ZERO JavaScript, and the site already ships a working pattern for it. Unlike /where — where the highlight responds to a click — the muscles worked by an exercise never change. Each of the 873 pages has exactly one answer, known at build time. So the whole figure, highlights already applied, can be emitted as inline SVG in the static HTML. The ~90% of traffic that never runs JS gets the identical picture as everyone else. That is the single most important design consequence in this spec, and it also keeps the diagram out of the 12.6 MB JS payload already on the open-defects list.

WHAT THE 380x440 ASSET ACTUALLY IS (I read it rather than assuming, because the shoulder-arm agent asserted no 2D diagram existed and that error propagated through its entire drawable_regions section). window.RNAWIKI_DATA.bodyZones: viewBox '0 0 380 440'; figures {front:{ox:10}, back:{ox:200}}; a 10-shape silhouette (head ellipse cx80 cy40 rx23 ry27; neck rect 18x14 at y63; torso rect 62x92 at y75; pelvis rect 54x44 at y156; two arm rects 17x118 at y80; two leg rects 22x182 at y194; two foot ellipses at cy386) on a 0..180 base per figure; and 15 zones — 10 front (neck, shoulders, chest, elbow, wrist, hip, thigh, knee, shin, ankle-foot), 5 back (upper-back, low-back, glutes, hamstring, calf). window.RNAWIKI_DATA.bodyWhereSvg is the prebuilt 9,007-character SVG of exactly that, and bodyWhereIndex is a 5,190-character HTML text twin. Both are inlined into site/where.html at build time by build/parse.js — I confirmed 20 bw-sil shapes and 25 bw-hit targets present in the static file.

EXTEND OR REPLACE — the answer is BOTH, split cleanly: REUSE the geometry and the accessibility scaffolding; REPLACE the zones array. Reasons, all measured from the asset:
  (a) The 15 zones are PAIN LOCATORS, not muscle outlines. Every one is an ellipse, and they carry problemIds — 'Wrist & forearm' is a 9x12 ellipse at cy184, sitting at the wrist end of the arm, not over the forearm belly. 'Shoulders' is a 12x10 ellipse on the joint. Recolouring these for a muscle map would put highlights on joints.
  (b) Only 5 zones have any muscle meaning at all (chest, thigh, hamstring, calf, glutes) and exactly ONE carries a muscleGroup field — chest. So 12 of the 17 muscle strings have no zone to land on: biceps, triceps, lats, traps, middle back, abdominals, adductors, abductors, forearms, neck-as-muscle, lower back as a muscle rather than a pain site, shoulders as a muscle.
  (c) Editing bodyZones.zones in place would break /where, because those zones are the join into problemIds. Add a sibling `muscleZones` array in data/body_zones.json (the editable source) alongside the existing `zones`.
  (d) Both figures are geometrically IDENTICAL — the back figure is the front figure translated by ox=190, not mirrored or redrawn. That is fine for a symmetrical outline and is why front-vs-back can be expressed purely by which figure a shape is placed on.
  (e) SIZE FLOOR, measured not guessed. One figure is 180 of a 380-unit viewBox. At a 380 CSS px map (scale 1.0) the arm is 17px wide, the leg 22px, the torso 62x92, the deltoid cap about 21x27. At 340 px (scale 0.895) the arm is 15px. So: at >=380 px render all Layer 1 regions plus Layer 2; between 300 and 380 px suppress inner-thigh, outer-hip and serratus and collapse interscapular into trapezius; below 300 px render ONE figure at a time with a view toggle, or drop to the text list. Publish this floor as a rule, because every sub-part region in this spec dies quietly below it.

WHAT A SCREEN READER GETS. Do NOT reuse /where's interactive pattern here — that page's shapes are aria-hidden with a parallel bw-hit layer of role="button" tabindex="0" elements, correct for a clickable map and wrong for a static one. For the exercise diagram:
  1. The SVG carries role="img" with a single <title> that states the whole answer as a sentence — e.g. 'Body map: the barbell bench press mainly works the chest, and also the shoulder cap and the back of the upper arm.' Per-shape <title> elements are pointless under role="img" and should be omitted.
  2. Better still, and my recommendation: make the SVG aria-hidden="true" outright and put the authoritative answer in a normal HTML list immediately after it — 'Mainly working: chest. Also working: front of the shoulder, back of the upper arm.' A picture is an aid; on a health page the accurate answer should be words, and words are what survive every failure mode at once (no JS, no images, no colour vision, screen reader, crawler, and the reader who simply cannot parse the outline).
  3. Never encode primary-versus-secondary in hue alone. Primary = solid fill; secondary = outline or reduced opacity; plus the stretch/SMR treatments above. That is four states on two channels, and it survives greyscale printing and the site's dark theme.
  4. Zero tab stops. Nothing on this diagram is actionable, so nothing should be focusable. If you later link a region to /muscle/<id>, put those links in the text list where they are already keyboard-reachable, not on SVG shapes.

WHAT A NO-JS READER GETS: the full inline SVG with highlights baked in, plus the text list — identical information to a JS reader, because there is nothing dynamic to lose. The text list is also the crawlable surface, which matters given the site's existing indexing work. The one thing to copy verbatim from bodyWhereIndex is that its links are real <a href> elements while its bw-find controls are <button>s that need JS; keep every navigational affordance on the <a> side.

ONE THING THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET AND SHOULD BE PLANNED FOR: there is no per-exercise page in the repo at all. site/muscle/ has 17 pages; site/body/ has only leg.html; site/bodymap.js is the Three.js/BodyParts3D engine, lazily imported and gated behind canRun3D(), and it is keyed on FMA id — note that the biceps-brachii structures row has an EMPTY fma field, so an FMA-keyed join fails on one of the most-used regions in this spec. The 2D diagram is the floor and the 3D is the enhancement, exactly as bodymap.js's own header comment already says.
not_confident_about: THE PIXEL FLOOR. My size thresholds (380 CSS px for all regions, 300 px to start suppressing, one-figure-at-a-time below that) are computed from the measured bodyZones geometry, which I did read — but I did not render the SVG and look at it, and I did not check site/styles.css for the container width /where actually uses. A 6 CSS px inner-thigh strip is my arithmetic, not an observed result. Verify against a real render before committing to inner-thigh, outer-hip and serratus as separate shapes; they are the three most likely to be unreadable.

THE DEADLIFT AND CLEAN FAMILY SPLITS ARE PROVEN INCONSISTENCIES, NOT PROVEN ERRORS. I can show from the repo that 26 deadlift rows get three different primaries and 41 clean/snatch rows get five. I cannot tell you which one is right, and I deliberately did not try: the shoulder-arm reviewer established that %MVIC is a within-muscle index that cannot rank force contribution between muscles, and that PMID 37229415's own conclusion declines to rank. Any 'correct' primary for the conventional deadlift is a curatorial decision the site has to own, not something the literature will hand over.

THE ARBITRARY-VERSUS-DEFENSIBLE LINE INSIDE THE SPLIT FAMILIES IS MY JUDGEMENT. I called Board_Press, Pin_Presses and the floor presses defensible as triceps-primary (ROM-restricted to the lockout) and the four full-ROM presses arbitrary; I called Romanian and stiff-legged deadlifts defensible as hamstring-primary and conventional-versus-trap-bar arbitrary. Those calls rest on movement description and coaching convention, not on a measurement, and a strength coach could redraw the line.

LATERAL PLYOMETRICS TAGGED ADDUCTORS. Lateral_Bound, Lateral_Box_Jump, Lateral_Cone_Hops and Carioca_Quick_Step are adductors-primary. I could not find evidence either way and I am NOT listing them as bad tagging. The adductors do contribute to the push-off in lateral bounding, so the tag is arguable rather than obviously wrong. Do not treat these as validated; do not treat them as defects.

LOADED CARRIES. Farmers_Walk, Rickshaw_Carry, Car_Drivers and Kneeling_Arm_Drill are forearms-primary. The shoulder-arm agent marked these could-not-check and I found nothing to change that — no EMG study ranking forearm flexors against upper trapezius in a loaded carry. Grip is the conventional failure point, which makes the tag defensible; the upper trapezius is under continuous high isometric load and is listed only as secondary. Unresolved.

PMID 8082611 (the trapezius needle-EMG study) IS SECOND-HAND IN THIS SPEC. It came from the vocabulary agent, the shoulder-arm agent repeated it, and its reviewer read it and found it says the superior trapezius is active in BOTH elevation and lowering — which contradicts the use the shoulder-arm agent made of it. I have relied on the reviewer's reading and on StatPearls NBK518994, which I did fetch. I did not read PMID 8082611 myself.

I RECEIVED ONLY TWO OF THE SIX REGIONAL REPORTS IN FULL. The shoulder-arm report and its audit arrived complete; the vocabulary report was truncated mid-finding; the other four never arrived. Everything I say about the trunk and the legs is my own recomputation from site/exercises.js and my own source-checking, NOT a reconciliation of their findings. If those four reports contain region-specific defects in the abdominals, back, hip or leg tags that I did not independently rediscover, this spec does not carry them. That is the biggest gap in this document and it should be closed before the sidecar is authored.

THE 13-EXCEPTION COUNT IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING. It is the set I could prove wrong from each exercise's own instruction text plus a cited anatomy source. I read the instructions[] of roughly 60 exercises out of 873. A full read of all 873 would very likely find more, particularly in the plyometrics (61) and strongman (21) categories, which I sampled only lightly and which are the two shelves where whole-body movements get a single arbitrary primary.

'MIDDLE BACK VS TRAPS' OWNERSHIP IS A DECISION I AM RECOMMENDING, NOT DERIVING. The nested-shape resolution (trapezius fills, interscapular outlines inside it) is a design proposal. The underlying facts are verified — the two authored pages both claim the middle trapezius, and StatPearls NBK534856 confirms the rhomboids are immediately deep to the trapezius — but a different resolution (give trapezius only the upper fibres and let middle back own the interscapular area) is also coherent and would need the traps page rewritten to match. Someone has to choose.

Structural facts that shape the diagram:
- EVERY exercise has exactly one primary muscle. primaryMuscles length distribution is {1: 873}. There is never a second primary. The diagram therefore always has exactly one primary region and 0–10 secondary regions.
- 272 exercises have an EMPTY secondaryMuscles array (213 strengthen, 42 stretch, 17 mobility). Roughly a third of pages will show a primary highlight and nothing else. That is a design case, not a bug.
- secondaryMuscles length distribution: 0:272, 1:140, 2:180, 3:133, 4:46, 5:46, 6:22, 7:19, 8:7, 9:4, 10:4.
- 9 exercises list the SAME muscle in both primaryMuscles and secondaryMuscles (All_Fours_Quad_Stretch, Barbell_Step_Ups, Bent-Arm_Barbell_Pullover, Clean_and_Press, Hurdle_Hops, Kneeling_Hip_Flexor, Snatch_Deadlift, Split_Snatch, Upper_Back_Stretch). The renderer needs an explicit precedence rule or these will paint twice / flicker between primary and secondary colour.

AUTHORED PAGES: 17 in window.RNAWIKI_DATA.anatomy.muscles — abdominals (Abdominals), abductors (Hip abductors), adductors (Hip adductors), biceps (Biceps brachii), calves (Calves), chest (Chest (pectorals)), forearms (Forearms), glutes (Glutes), hamstrings (Hamstrings), lats (Lats (latissimus dorsi)), lower-back (Lower back (erector spinae)), middle-back (Middle back), neck (Neck), quadriceps (Quadriceps), shoulders (Shoulders (deltoids)), traps (Trapezius), triceps (Triceps brachii).

MAPPING — BOTH DIRECTIONS, COMPLETE. The two vocabularies are 1:1 and total. Zero exercise-DB muscles lack an authored page. Zero authored pages are untagged by any exercise. The only divergence is slug form: exercise-DB "lower back"/"middle back" (space) vs authored ids "lower-back"/"middle-back" (hyphen), and that gap is bridged by a db_name field present on exactly those 2 of 17 records.

RESOLUTION (site/app.js:82): `const muscleByName = {}; (ANAT.muscles || []).forEach(m => muscleByName[m.db_name || m.id] = m);` — keyed on db_name when present, else id. I simulated it against the real data: 17 of 17 distinct strings resolve, 0 FAIL. Consumers at app.js:8914 (exercise card, .filter(mn => muscleByName[mn]) then .slice(0,3) — the slice is dead code since primaryMuscles is always length 1) and app.js:9561–9563 (detail-page chips, falls back to a non-linking <span class="tag-chip static"> on miss). So today the link layer is correct and complete. It is however load-bearing on two hand-written db_name values with no test; see finding on fragility.

THE ACTUAL RISK IS NOT THE MAPPING — IT IS THE VOCABULARY. The mapping is clean; the words are not. Of the 17 strings, only 5 denote a single muscle (biceps, triceps, lats, traps, and arguably neck-as-region). The other 12 are regions or functional groups, and 6 of them span BOTH the front and back of the body or span superficial and deep layers. A one-blob-per-string diagram is anatomically wrong on a large, countable fraction of pages — worst case "calves", where 8 exercises name muscles on the FRONT and OUTSIDE of the shin while the tag would paint the BACK of the calf.

Repo asset worth knowing about: window.RNAWIKI_DATA.structures holds 43 sub-muscles with FMA ids, per-structure region labels (e.g. thigh-anterior, shoulder-posterior, forearm-anterior, chest-deep), confidence and secondSourceVerified flags, indexed by groupId. That is already the disambiguation layer this diagram needs — it resolves 15 of the 17 group names into drawable sub-parts. Note it carries an 18th groupId, "tibialis-anterior" (FMA:22532, region lower-leg-anterior), which has NO authored muscle page and NO exercise-DB string — it is exactly the structure the "calves" mis-tagging needs.

final_verdict.headline: Build it, but only at exactly the resolution the data has — 17 regions whose ids ARE the 17 tags, no sub-splits, suppressed on 14 named pages, rendered small and second to the movement photo the repo already ships on all 873 pages.
final_verdict.reasoning:
VERIFICATION FIRST. I recomputed everything from site/exercises.js and site/data.js with node+vm rather than inheriting any number. The founder's figures are exact: 250 distinct pictures, 720/873 (82.5%) shared, 17 pictures if primary-only. I added three numbers nobody in the dossier computed, and one of them nearly changed my verdict.

(a) The top 17 pictures cover 50% of the entire corpus.
(b) Mean regions lit per page is 2.95, not the 4.79 one reviewer measured — that was their glute-heavy subset. 275 pages light exactly ONE region; only 17% light 5+. The "silhouette with eleven of seventeen regions coloured in" failure is real but rare (3 pages hit 11).
(c) THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS MOST, and it is the strongest anti-diagram fact in existence: the repo ships an `alternatives` field on 827 exercises, 4,404 alternative pairs. 1,597 of them — 36.3% — render a BYTE-IDENTICAL picture. The site says "try this instead" and the diagram cannot show any difference on more than a third of those recommendations.

(2) DOES "ONE TOKEN CANNOT DRIVE A SPATIAL CLAIM" DEFEAT THE DIAGRAM? It bounds it, hard, and it kills every proposal in the dossier — but it does not defeat a diagram drawn at token resolution. The reviewers are right that `glutes` resolves identically on all 242 of its exercises to {maximus, medius, minimus}; I confirmed the `structures` registry keys on groupId, so no exercise can ever reach a sub-structure. Any three-deltoid-head or rectus-vs-oblique split is therefore generated by the renderer, not read from the data — the site inventing a fact and painting it confidently. That is disqualifying, and it disqualifies all six auditors' proposed region lists (7, 7, 13, 9, 5, 4 regions). But the argument proves "no shape finer than a token," not "no shape." A region whose id IS the token makes precisely the token's claim and adds one thing the token does not contain: WHERE. For a reader who does not know the word "lats," the word carries zero location and the shape carries all of it. That gain is real, it is the only gain, and it is available at zero invention cost.

Two of my own verifications show this boundary doing useful work. Scapular_Pull-Up is tagged traps and its text says "depressing your shoulder girdle in a reverse shrugging motion" — lower traps. An auditor called this a blocking directional inversion. At sub-tag resolution it is: an upper-trap blob highlights the antagonist. At tag resolution "traps" is simply correct. The finding is an argument FOR coarse, not against drawing. Same with Piriformis-SMR, whose own instructions say "until you feel tension in your upper glute."

(3) THE 82% COLLISION. This is the question I spent longest on, and my answer is that the collision number does not kill the diagram — it tells you what the diagram is for, and therefore how much of the page it may occupy. Differentiating this exercise from the next one is a job the diagram cannot do and does not need to do: the `image` field is populated on 873/873 exercises with a photo of the actual movement, and the name and instructions are on the page. Answering "where is that on my body" is a per-READER question, not a per-exercise one — a reader lands on one page and never sees the 46 as a set. A fact that is constant across 46 pages is still a fact the reader needs on the page they are on.

But that reframe carries an obligation, and it is the whole of my "smaller." If the picture is invariant across 46 exercises, it is a per-muscle fact borrowed onto an exercise page. So it must never be the page's hero image, must never sit above the photo, must be roughly chip-sized, and must be a NAVIGATION surface — tap a lit region, go to /muscle/<id> — rather than an assertion surface. That last idea is the best thing in the twelve reports (it comes from the reviewer who otherwise voted NO) and it converts the repeat from an embarrassment into the point: the same shape appearing on 46 chest pages is a consistent, learnable index into one rich destination. The 36.3% alternatives collision is then a labelling requirement, not a veto: never caption the diagram in a way that implies it distinguishes the alternatives.

(4) THE VISUAL-LEARNER REQUIREMENT. This is a real constraint and I am not arguing it away, but it does not adjudicate resolution — and the honest reading is that it is already better served than the brief assumes. The repo ships, today: a movement photo on all 873 pages; 17 authored muscle pages each carrying 3-4 hand-built animated `action_figures` (I read the abdominals SVGs — trunk flexion drawn as a spine curling into a C, side view, with motion); a Sketchfab `model_embed` on all 17; and 43 `structures` records with `plainName`, `palpation` and a `locate` field that is genuinely outstanding for a visual, hands-on learner ("Sit down and straighten one leg hard so the thigh tightens: the soft teardrop-shaped bulge that pops up just above your kneecap..."). The visual requirement is met by routing to that material, not by inventing per-exercise geometry. A visual learner is not served by a picture that is wrong, and is actively harmed by one that is confidently wrong, because a picture is retained as a fact in a way a sentence is not. So: give him a picture, make it coarse, make it a door.

(5) WHY NOT "DO NOT BUILD", given three reviewers said no. I read all six reviewer verdicts closely and none of them actually says "no figure ever." The abdominals reviewer says build "a single non-subdivided abdominal wall region, front view, lit as one shape, linking through to the muscle page." The chest/back reviewer says keep a coarse silhouette "at the zone granularity the repo already has." The arms/shoulders reviewer says "a labelled list should lead; a diagram may support it." Those three descriptions and my recommendation are the same artifact. The apparent 3-3 split is an artifact of each reviewer answering "should we build the 7-to-13-region thing my auditor proposed" — and the answer to that is unanimously no, including from me.

(6) BUILDABILITY. The infrastructure is already 60% there and nobody in the dossier checked it correctly. site/data.js contains `bodyZones`: viewBox 380x440, two figures (front ox=10, back ox=200) on a 0..180 base, a 10-shape silhouette, and 15 named zones — and one zone (`chest`) already carries a `muscleGroup` binding, which is exactly the hook this feature needs. Nine of my seventeen regions already exist as zones (chest, glutes, hamstring→hamstrings, calf→calves, thigh→quadriceps, low-back→lower back, neck, shoulders, wrist→forearms). Seven need new ellipses. The schema is ellipse-only, which is a feature here: it makes fine geometry literally unexpressible, enforcing the resolution ceiling in the data format. At a 340px container each figure is ~161 CSS px, the chest zone is ~39x27px, the arm rects 15px wide. That comfortably holds 17 group shapes and cannot hold 43 sub-shapes — the reviewers' geometry objection is correct and is satisfied by stopping at 17.

CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDITS I VERIFIED MYSELF (accuracy was the requirement, so these matter):
- Lower_Back_Curl, called "the single most flagrant wrong answer": the tag is CORRECT. kind=stretch, and under the repo's consistent stretch convention primary = muscle lengthened. Prone extension lengthens the abs. Its reviewer was right, the auditor was wrong.
- Chair_Lower_Back_Stretch, called an upstream freebie error: "bend to one side with your arm over your head" is a textbook lat stretch. Tag is fine.
- Rear_Leg_Raises, called "the single worst diagram failure available": its own text says "The knee and hip should both extend." Knee extension IS quadriceps. This is a missing-glutes secondary, not a front/back inversion. Materially overstated.
- Side_Leg_Raises: the swing "back down, allowing it to cross the opposite leg" is adduction. Defensible.
- CONFIRMED as genuine: Band_Hip_Adductions is loaded ABduction tagged adductors. Smith_Machine_Reverse_Calf_Raises has heels on the platform and balls hanging off — "raise the balls of your feet" is dorsiflexion; "flexing your calf" in the same sentence is copied boilerplate. Dumbbell_Lying_Pronation/Supination describe prone shoulder external rotation, not forearm rotation. Front_Cone_Hops_or_hurdle_hops and Hurdle_Hops carry byte-identical 5-muscle secondary arrays with opposite primaries, and Hurdle_Hops lists hamstrings in both slots.
- Also verified: 9 exercises list their primary muscle in secondaryMuscles too, so the renderer needs an explicit precedence rule (primary wins) or those regions will paint twice.

Anterior_Tibialis-SMR — VERIFIED: 'apply pressure to the muscles on the outside of your shins'. Front of the leg, tagged calves.
Peroneals-SMR — VERIFIED: side-lying, 'roller placed on the outside of your lower leg'. Lateral compartment, not the posterior calf.
Peroneals_Stretch — same lateral compartment (evertors), tagged calves.

Posterior_Tibialis_Stretch — correct side, wrong layer. Deepest muscle of the deep posterior compartment, no surface footprint; its only landmark is a tendon behind the medial ankle. A lit calf bulge tells the reader they are stretching a muscle they are not.

Foot-SMR — VERIFIED: 'stretches the fascia of the muscles in the feet... across the arch of your foot'. Tagged calves. The sole of the foot has no zone on either figure and cannot get one on this silhouette.
