That is shoulder external rotation (infraspinatus, teres minor, posterior scapula), tagged forearms. Wrong segment of the limb despite the exercise's own name.

Band_Hip_Adductions — VERIFIED: 'Keeping the knee straight, raise your right legs out to the side as far as you can', kind=strengthen, band resists. Loaded hip ABduction tagged adductors PRIMARY with an empty secondary. A true antagonist inversion: the inner thigh would light for a movement driven by the outer hip.
Balance_Board — 'Stand up on it and try to balance.' No prime mover exists to highlight; which muscle dominates depends entirely on the board axis and task.
Ankle_Circles — circumduction is by definition sequential dorsiflexion, inversion, plantarflexion and eversion. Recruits all four compartments in turn; any single highlight is a guess.

Knee_Circles — standing knee circumduction with feet planted, tagged calves primary. Neither of the calf's two actions drives it. (Note: I do NOT extend this to Arm_Circles, Shoulder_Circles, Elbow_Circles, Wrist_Circles or the hip circles — those resolve to a group that genuinely surrounds the joint being circled, so they are coarse-correct and keep their figure.)

Stomach_Vacuum — VERIFIED: its own text describes a 20-second isometric contraction while kind='stretch'. Target is transversus abdominis, the deepest of the three wall muscles, with no surface footprint at all. Wrong layer AND wrong contraction type.
final_verdict.stretch_handling:
This is the single highest-value accuracy fix in the whole build and it is nearly free: it touches 123 of 873 pages (91 stretch, 32 mobility) and requires no new geometry.

THE PROBLEM, which five of six audits found independently and I confirmed: primaryMuscles means the CONTRACTING prime mover on the 750 strengthen rows and the muscle being LENGTHENED on most stretch rows. Same field, opposite physiology. One fill colour with one legend is therefore literally false on ~123 pages, and the sign is inverted rather than merely vague — on Calf_Stretch_Hands_Against_Wall the calf is not working, it is being pulled long.

THE RULE:
1. Stretch and mobility get a DIFFERENT VISUAL TREATMENT, not the same fill with a different caption. Strengthen = solid warm fill, verb "Works". Stretch = cool diagonal-hatched fill, verb "Lengthens". Mobility = same hatch, verb "Mobilises". A reader must be able to tell the two apart without reading, because the whole reason to draw a picture is that pictures are read pre-verbally.
2. The verb must be rendered from `kind` as a literal string next to the figure, so the legend is per-page and cannot be globally false.
3. DO NOT trust `kind` as a physiological classifier beyond that. I verified it is a coarse derived field and it misfires in both directions: Stomach_Vacuum is kind='stretch' but is an isometric contraction (suppressed above); Superman is a stretch-family row whose text says "Squeeze your lower back"; Scissor_Kick is kind='mobility' but is strength work; Split_Squats is kind='mobility' but is a jumping split lunge. The hedge that makes this safe is wording: "Lengthens" and "Mobilises" are both true of a tissue under a foam roller and of a tissue held at length, and neither asserts a direction of force. Do not upgrade to "Stretches: the muscle being pulled long" — that specific claim fails on the 13 SMR rows, where the tissue is being compressed under a roller, and on the active stretches.
4. Dynamic_Chest_Stretch is the one page where primary and secondary carry OPPOSITE mechanical roles inside a single record — the pec is lengthening while the scapular retractors concentrically contract. Two-colour rendering will show these as the same kind of event. Accept it, or add it to the suppression list; I would accept it, since the coarse regions are both correct as locations.
final_verdict.instead_or_alongside:
ALONGSIDE — the diagram is the smallest of five things on the page, and four of the five already exist in the repo. Ordered by vertical position:

1. THE MOVEMENT PHOTO (already built, zero work). Every one of the 873 exercises has a populated `image` field pointing at a free-exercise-db photo of the movement itself. This is the per-exercise visual, it is 873/873 distinct, and it belongs above the diagram. It is what actually answers "what is this exercise" for a visual learner. The diagram must never displace it.

2. THE MUSCLE LIST, WHICH LEADS ON CONTENT (already built). site/app.js already renders primaryMuscles and secondaryMuscles as chips hyperlinked to /muscle/<id>. Restyle into two labelled rows — "Prime mover" and "Also listed" — with the second deliberately hedged. This matters because I confirmed the secondaries are partly boilerplate, not observation: Front_Cone_Hops_or_hurdle_hops and Hurdle_Hops carry byte-identical five-muscle secondary arrays while disagreeing on the primary, and 45 lower-body exercises share the identical quadriceps+[calves,glutes,hamstrings] signature. A tint and a chip look equally authoritative; only words can say "listed as" rather than "measured". The list is the source of truth; the diagram is its index.

3. THE DIAGRAM, small, below both, as a NAVIGATION surface. Both figures always visible — never a front view with a flip control, since 173 of 226 lower-body exercises name muscles on both faces once secondaries count. Each lit region is a tap target to /muscle/<id>. Caption: "Where these muscles are" — a location claim, which the data supports — never "Muscles worked", which is a mechanism claim it does not.

4. THE 17 AUTHORED MUSCLE PAGES AS THE DESTINATION (already built, and much better than anything an exercise page could hold). I read them: each carries 3-4 hand-authored ANIMATED action_figures — the abdominals page alone separates trunk flexion, rotation, side-bending, compression and anti-movement as five distinct moving SVGs — plus a Sketchfab model_embed, plus prose that already states the corrections the auditors wanted ("Hip flexors (psoas/iliacus) — mistaking hip-flexor work for ab work is why many 'ab' exercises actually load the low back").

5. THE `structures` REGISTRY'S `locate` TEXT, surfaced on hover or on the muscle page. 43 records with plainName, palpation and a find-it-on-yourself instruction. For a hands-on visual learner this is the best asset in the repo and it is currently underused.

WHERE THE COARSE TAG IS KNOWN TO BE COARSER THAN THE TRUTH — piriformis under `glutes`, iliopsoas under `quadriceps` and `abdominals`, TFL versus glute med/min, tibialis anterior under `calves` — put the correction in per-exercise TEXT, where it can be curated one page at a time. Never in geometry, where one wrong shape is wrong identically 242 times.

ONE THING NOT TO DO: do not add an `iliopsoas` region to the diagram. Two audits pushed for it and the anatomy is right — it is the true prime mover in ~27 hanging-leg-raise-family rows and ~10 hip-flexor stretches. But it is retroperitoneal, has no surface footprint, and no exercise carries a tag that could select it. Add it as a `structures` record (FMA:64918) and name it in prose on the affected pages. A shape for it would be a confident lie about a place on the body.
not_confident_about: WHETHER 17 SHAPES EARN THEIR BUILD COST AT ALL. My verdict rests on the claim that location is information the token lacks. If the typical reader already knows roughly where lats and quads are, the diagram adds nothing and the honest answer flips to 'do not build' — the 36.3% alternatives collision would then be decisive. This is an empirical question about readers that no amount of repo analysis can settle, and I did not test it. If there is any way to check whether readers use the existing /where silhouette, do that before building the seven new ellipses.

THE OLYMPIC / KETTLEBELL CLASS, ~21 EXERCISES. Two-Arm_Kettlebell_Clean is tagged shoulders PRIMARY and I verified it has no overhead component — 'clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips'. The engine is hip and knee extension. Coarse rendering lights the shoulder solid with legs tinted, which is a ranking error rather than a location error, so I left the class off the suppression list. I am not confident that is right. If the founder wants zero misleading pages rather than zero wrong-location pages, this class (plus the 12 triceps-primary bench presses, where the reviewer showed the auditor's EMG citation does not support flipping them) should be suppressed too, taking the no-figure list from 14 to roughly 45.

MIDDLE-BACK VERSUS TRAPS. My 17-region list draws these as abutting shapes, but rhomboids genuinely lie deep to trapezius and 32 exercises carry both tags. A flat 2D tint has no vocabulary for 'underneath'. I called it an honest compromise; a stricter reading is that any interscapular boundary is an invented line and the two should be merged into one 'upper back' region, dropping the count to 16. The same argument applies weakly to lats-over-lumbar-erectors.

THE STRETCH-VERSUS-STRENGTHEN COUNT. I am confident the semantic inversion is real and that ~123 pages are affected, but not that hatching solves it. Four audits found rows where `kind` itself is wrong (Superman, Scissor_Kick, Split_Squats, Stomach_Vacuum), so a `kind`-driven legend inherits those errors. I mitigated with deliberately weak verbs, but I did not audit all 123 rows myself — I read roughly 25.

SECONDARY-MUSCLE TINTING. I recommend tinting secondaries, but the byte-identical five-muscle arrays are strong evidence that secondaries are template-generated. A defensible stricter build tints nothing and draws only the primary — which drops the corpus to 17 distinct pictures and makes the collision problem far worse while making the accuracy problem far better. I chose signal over purity here and I hold that loosely.

SEVERAL AUDIT FINDINGS I DID NOT INDEPENDENTLY CHECK, particularly the EMG-citation disputes. The reviewers refuted specific PMIDs in at least eight places (PMID 39764299, 33561137, 35992501, 37229415, a misquoted StatPearls sentence on the sternocostal head, and a fabricated 59-of-91 statistic). Every one of those refutations that I could test against the repo held up, which raises my confidence in the reviewers generally and lowers it in the auditors' external citations. But I verified repo facts, not literature, and none of my recommendation depends on any EMG claim — which is deliberate, and is also why I think a coarse diagram is defensible where a fine one would not be.

I did not verify that the exercise page renderer can cheaply consume bodyZones. I confirmed bodyZones lives in site/data.js and is prebuilt into bodyWhereSvg + bodyWhereIndex by build/parse.js for site/where.html, and that exactly one zone (chest) already carries a muscleGroup binding. I did not trace the exercise-detail render path, so the integration cost is an estimate.

adversarial_challenge.strongest_objection:
The verdict spends its entire budget on WHAT to draw and never checks WHETHER THE PAGE IS SERVED TO ANYONE. It is a resolution argument about a surface that currently has no document, no index entry, no sitemap row, and no inbound link.

Verified in /Users/admin/ClaudeRepo/Claude Projects/rnawiki:

1. `server.js` line 3619: `const NOINDEX_SHELL_ROUTES = ['exercise', 'fork', 'fuel@3'];` — the exercise route is explicitly noindexed.
2. `site/sitemap.xml`: 564 URLs, of which **0** are exercise pages (171 /c, 124 /compare, 103 /target, 52 /protocol, 41 /problem, 17 /muscle, 16 /pathway, 16 /goal ... zero /exercise).
3. There is no `site/exercise/` directory. No exercise page is prerendered. The repo's own comment above that constant: exercise and fork were "MEASURED live 2026-08-11: 200, no X-Robots-Tag ... ~90% of traffic never runs JavaScript, so for almost every requester these URLs are duplicate-content soft 404s," followed by "The honest fix for all three is a prerendered document with real content. Until one exists, the document that IS served must not invite indexing."
4. I grepped every prerendered document in `site/` for a link to an exercise page: **zero**. The 17 indexed muscle pages carry 307 exercise references but not one `href` to `/exercise/<id>`. The only links that exist are `#/exercise/${esc(e.id)}` emitted by `site/app.js` at runtime.

So a diagram built here renders for roughly one requester in ten and receives no organic entry at all. The verdict's own closing line is exactly where this hid: "I did not trace the exercise-detail render path, so the integration cost is an estimate."
